subject: CurieBank: conditional commitment for activation + SLA spec
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CurieBank activation: ask for product decision

Team,

CurieBank is asking for a conditional activation commitment tied to the SOW they just sent (attached). This is the gating item for procurement — they will sign the PO if we provide a written commitment on the activation SLA and warm-pool behavior. The commercial ask is straightforward: 99.9% uptime, P99 < 500ms for their production traffic pattern (approx 1k RPS peak for conversational inference), and a warm pool with pre-seeded KV cache for their tenant on go-live.

Why this is urgent:
- Procurement needs a technical commitment by EOD next Wednesday (Apr 28) to include in the contract.
- The account is a potential $1.2M ARR over 12 months.

What I need from Product/Engineering:
- Feasibility: can we commit to the SLA/latency numbers and warm-pool behavior for a single-tenant reserved profile?
- Scope: what's the minimal implementation (config + infra + rollout) to satisfy the ask?
- Cost/tradeoffs: any additional commitments (reserved capacity, compute premiums, activation windows) we should bake into the commercial terms?

I've attached the SOW excerpt the customer shared.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Rep, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: curie_sow_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CurieBank activation: ask for product decision

Thanks for the context, Ben. 

High level response: we can probably offer a conditional commitment, but we need to be explicit about the constraints and acceptance criteria. Before we promise anything to Procurement, please confirm the following from the customer:
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrency (not just RPS).
2) Average and max input sequence lengths and typical prompt/response token counts.
3) Whether they require session affinity / sticky KV cache semantics across requests.

Preliminary product questions I need Engineering to answer:
- Can we guarantee P99 < 500ms under the stated workload on a dedicated pool with a warm cache? If so, what capacity cushion (GPU count / reservation) is required?
- Is there a minimal feature work (API + routing flag + admin config) we must ship to provide the warm-pool + pre-seed behavior described?
- Operational asks: runbooks, monitoring hooks, and a rollback plan if latency degrades.

Connor/Laura: can you sketch a minimal spec and an estimate (effort + lead time) for a customer-scoped activation that meets the ask? If an engineering workaround is required (e.g., dedicated warm instances + soft quota), call that out clearly so Sales can include it in commercial terms.

I opened ENG-1234 for the tracking placeholder (link below). Please put a rough ETA in this thread — procurement is driving the timeline.

Olga
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-1234

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@curiebank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@curiebank.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CurieBank activation: ask for product decision

Ben — thanks for escalating. Procurement is watching the SOW timeline and would like a written note from Redwood that describes the activation behavior we will rely on. Excerpt from our SOW: 

- Production SLA target: 99.9% monthly uptime for tenant-specific inference endpoints.
- Latency target: P99 <= 500ms for requests with payloads up to 2k tokens; average workload during business hours expected ~600 RPS, with peak bursts up to 1k RPS for brief windows.
- Warm pool: Redwood should provide a tenant-specific warm pool seeded with model and KV cache prior to go-live; warm-pool should be able to scale to handle the first 5 minutes of traffic without cold starts.

We can be flexible on implementation as long as the behavior is achieved. Procurement would ideally see an agreed technical approach by end of day Apr 28 to proceed with signatures.

I've attached the SOW page with the relevant clauses. Happy to hop on a call to walk through.

—Tom Reynolds
Head of AI Engineering, CurieBank
[Attachment: curie_sow_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CurieBank activation: ask for product decision

On Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 08:05 Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@curiebank.com> wrote:
> Ben — thanks for escalating. Procurement is watching the SOW timeline and would like a written note from Redwood that describes the activation behavior we will rely on.
> (SOW excerpt pasted)

Engineering read: the ask is feasible but not "out of box" for hosted multi-tenant. To meet the behavior reliably we need a scoped customer-reserved profile with a small set of product changes + infra reservation. Summary below.

Proposed minimal spec (scoped, deliverable in parallel to legal):
- Dedicated activation profile: tenant pinning to a reserved compute pool for the first 72 hours post-go-live. This avoids noisy neighbor variance and gives predictable CPU/GPU availability.
- Warm pool semantics: ability to pre-provision N instances (configurable) with pre-loaded KV cache and model weights; control plane flag to enable/disable pre-seeding per-tenant.
- Acceptance criteria (for contract): P99 < 500ms for the first 1000 RPS steady at launch on the reserved pool, as measured by our production telemetry and customer-provided test harness.
- Operational deliverables: runbook, dashboards (token-level latency, warm-pool hit rate), and a 2-week post-launch observation window with rollback triggers.

Estimated effort & timeline:
- Product + config work: 2 weeks (small API + admin UI toggles).
- Core runtime changes (warm pool pre-seed + tenancy config): 3–4 weeks.
- Infra & QA + manual canary: 1–2 weeks.
Total: 6–8 weeks for fully automated, production-grade rollout. We can do a manual pilot faster (~2 weeks) if the customer accepts manual ops steps and a documented runbook.

Cost/tradeoff notes:
- This will require reserved capacity billing for the activation window (we should include an activation fee / bump in the PO).
- There is operational risk for the first 72 hours; we recommend a service credit schedule if SLOs degrade but that should be scoped in the contract.

Next steps:
1) Olga/Product: confirm which of the three commitment levels we send to Procurement — (A) Written conditional commitment + manual pilot (2 weeks), (B) Written commitment with ETA 6–8 weeks + reserved-billing clause, or (C) decline to commit and offer alternative SLA metrics.
2) Ben/Sales: align commercial language for reserved billing and activation fee.
3) Connor/Eng: if (B) chosen, we need ENG-1234 prioritization — estimate put into Jira and delivery owner assigned.

I attached a short draft spec for the activation behavior that Product can use to respond to Procurement.

Laura Bennett
Staff Engineer, Runtime Services
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_commit_spec.md (text/markdown)]
